results.name: Persona-Story Alignment
results.reasoning: All user stories correctly map to their personas: encryption/key rotation/CLI config under Cloud Infrastructure Admin, backend selection under Cloud Provider Admin, secrets API management under Tenant Admin, and credential retrieval under Tenant User; no internal system stories exist and no sanitization stories appear under Cloud Provider Admin.
quotes: As a Cloud Infrastructure Admin, I want secrets encrypted at rest
As a Cloud Provider Admin, I want to select between database-backed storage
As a Tenant Admin, I want to store and manage secrets

results.name: In Scope / Out of Scope Accuracy
results.reasoning: The generated document's In Scope and Out of Scope sections differ significantly from the gold standard: it omits many gold In Scope items (service coverage scope, installation, E2E testing, documentation, self-service secret creation, automatic secret creation, tenant-scoped privilege isolation) and incorrectly places items like 'External secret manager integration (Vault)' in Out of Scope when gold treats Vault as a prerequisite In Scope item; it also adds scope-creep items not in gold (CLI support for encryption key configuration, per-project encryption key management).
quotes: Installation — cloud provider must deploy and configure a Vault-compatible secret store as a prerequisite
E2E testing — secret CRUD
External secret manager integration (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) — deferred to a future enhancement

results.name: Design Leakage
results.reasoning: The generated document contains no internal implementation details like controller names, reconciler logic, finalizer behavior, CRD field names, or agent/InfraEnv terminology; references to 'OPA policies', 'envelope encryption', 'hub secret backend', and 'SecretReference type' are borderline but represent acceptable product-level vocabulary rather than internal implementation specifics.
quotes: hub (Kubernetes) secret backend
SecretReference type used to replace ad-hoc secret retrieval RPCs
OPA policies

results.name: Problem Statement Quality
results.reasoning: The Problem Statement describes only user pain (unencrypted storage, database exposure, ad-hoc RPCs, forced bespoke implementations) and cost of inaction (credential exposure on compromise, bespoke work for new secret types), with no solution language.
quotes: stored as unencrypted fields within resource database tables
any database compromise exposes all tenant credentials
forcing every consuming service to implement its own retrieval mechanism

results.name: Async Status Visibility
results.reasoning: Neither the In Scope section nor the User Stories address async status visibility, progress tracking, or failure reason visibility for secret creation operations.
quotes: Dedicated secret resource with full CRUD operations

results.name: Content Completeness
results.reasoning: The generated document covers core concepts (encryption at rest, pluggable backends, uniform API, tenant isolation) but misses several substantive items: explicit service scope (BMaaS, CaaS, VMaaS, MaaS, Enclave), automatic secret creation during provisioning, self-service SSH key/OIDC secret creation, RBAC for tenant secret access control, E2E testing and documentation requirements, Vault-compatible store as the backend dependency, and multiple Tenant User stories (update, delete, list metadata).
